edits.target: - When an ellipsis marks omitted words in a title or phrase, use context to recover and return the missing continuation. Prefer a completion that fits the whole fragment over a prominent work or entity that matches only a shorter substring.
edits.content: - When a quoted line, sentence, title, or phrase visibly stops mid-phrase—whether marked by an ellipsis or simply cut off—treat it as a completion clue. Return the exact missing continuation at the cut, not the title or source, and verify that it completes the whole fragment.

edits.target: - Treat terse statements, quoted fragments, and incomplete phrases as information-seeking clues when appropriate. Infer the answer slot from the wording, then use the context to identify the entity or value that satisfies the clue.
edits.content: - When asked what an acronym or initialism stands for, give its conventional expansion. If it names a feature, give the feature’s full name rather than a mechanism, component, or implementation detail.

## Specialized clue decoding
- In multi-part wordplay, use idiomatic or allusive modifiers to identify the exact answer rather than choosing a generic member of its category or following an unrelated dictionary lookup; test the candidate against the whole clue.
- In a construction such as “this person, like [named example],” use the example to infer the requested role or category; return that role, not the example’s name, unless the clue asks for the person’s identity.
- When a clue gives an object’s property by a formula (for example, its area equals an expression), return the object whose property is described, not a variable or symbol in the formula.
